subject: Sampling Error on Multinomial Logistic Regression

messages.author: 8fc2bc9cca049463
messages.subject: Sampling Error on Multinomial Logistic Regression
parts:
Hi everyone,

I'm having an issue with a sampling error in the following model. The model compiles fine but continues to give the following error during sampling:

Informational Message: The parameter state is about to be Metropolis rejected due to the following underlying, non-fatal (really) issue (and please ignore that what comes next might say 'error'): Invalid value of prec: Error in function validate transformed params N4stan5agrad3varE: prec[1]  is 1.#QNAN:0, but must be greater than or equal to 0
If the problem persists across multiple draws, you might have a problem with an initial state or a gradient somewhere.
 If the problem does not persist, the resulting samples will still be drawn from the posterior.


It seems like there is an issue with prec[1], but this is a value that is set in advance (it is 1e-8), so I don't know why it is coming up as NAN? After a bit of running, the program just stops running altogether, and I get the following error:

Error : std::bad_alloc
error occurred during calling the sampler; sampling not done

I'm on Windows 7, running stan through R (rstan). Here's the model:

mult3_mod <- '
data {
  int<lower=0> I; //number of sites
  int<lower=0> J; //number of taxa
  int<lower=0> n[I]; //number of individuals identified 
  int<lower=0> c[I]; //number of cells picked
  int<lower=0> M[I]; // number of total cells possible
  vector[I] a; //total area sampled
  vector[I] logcond; //log(conductivity) value at each site
  int<lower=0> taxon_ct[I,J]; //count of taxon at each site
  real l_alpha_1; //set first taxon log alpha = 0
  real beta_1; //set first taxon beta = 0
  real prec_1; //set inverse variance to = 0.00000001 
}
parameters {
  vector<lower=0,upper=1>[I] tau;
  real mu_logalpha;
  real<lower=0> tau_logalpha;
  real mu_beta;
  real<lower=0> tau_beta;
  real<lower=0> rho;
  vector[J-1] beta_2;
  vector[J-1] log_alpha_2;
  vector<lower=0>[J-1] prec_2;
}
transformed parameters {
  vector[J] phi[I];
  vector[J] log_alpha;
  vector[J] beta;
  vector<lower=0>[J] prec;
  vector<lower=0>[J] gam;
  log_alpha[1] <- l_alpha_1;
  beta[1] <- beta_1;
  prec[1] <- prec_1;
  for (j in 2:J) {
    log_alpha[j] <- log_alpha_2[j-1];
    beta[j] <- beta_2[j-1];
    prec[j] <- prec_2[j-1];
  }
  for (j in 1:J){
    gam[j] <- pow(prec[j],-0.5);
    for(i in 1:I){
      phi[i,j] <- log_alpha[j] - square((beta[j] - logcond[i])/gam[j]);
    }
  }
}
model {
for(i in 1:I){
    c[i] ~ binomial(M[i],tau[i]);
    taxon_ct[i] ~ multinomial(softmax(phi[i]));
}
tau ~ beta(1,1);
mu_logalpha ~ normal(0,sqrt(1000));
tau_logalpha ~ uniform(0,100);
mu_beta ~ normal(0,sqrt(1000));
tau_beta ~ uniform(0,100);
rho ~ gamma(1,1);
log_alpha_2 ~ normal(mu_logalpha,tau_logalpha);
beta_2 ~ normal(mu_beta,tau_beta);
prec_2 ~ gamma(1, rho);
}
generated quantities {
  vector<lower=0>[J] alpha; 
  vector<lower=0>[J] density[I];
  alpha <- exp(log_alpha);
  for (i in 1:I){
      density[i] <- n[i]*M[i]/(c[i]*a[i])*softmax(phi[i]);
  }
}
'

Thanks in advance for any help you can provide. 

Kris

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Sampling Error on Multinomial Logistic Regression
parts:
The bad_alloc is most likely because you ran out of memory.
I'm not even sure if we can run 64-bit versions of Stan on
Windows, which has been a huge pain for us because of its
nonstandard C++ tool chain.

Was there a particular distribution cited in the informational
message? This isn't necessarily an error and can just signal
a Metropolis rejection. We are still trying to figure out how
to provide feedback for users on where errors might be without
confusing them thinking they're fatal if they don't persist.

You probably don't want to "set inverse variance to = 0.00000001"
unless your scale is very large.

- Bob

parts:
Hi Bob,

The weird thing is I have run something very similar to this model (the only new addition being the binomial sampling of cells) and the calculation of density in the generated quantities. Everything ran perfectly before (with the same parameters set for the first class of the multinomial). The only informational piece is what I already posted:
Invalid value of prec: Error in function validate transformed params N4stan5agrad3varE: prec[1]  is 1.#QNAN:0, but must be greater than or equal to 0

And again, since I set prec[1] initially (see my above code), I don't know why I would keep getting this error over and over.
 
The variance isn't really a variance in this case. I'm fitting a Gaussian response (typical of ecological gradients) to the data , but because of the identifiability issue with the multinomial parameters, I wanted to set the values for the main case based on what would be zero (or close to zero) if the Gaussian response was parameterized as a purely quadratic regression. So, the "inverse variance" parameter is actually a coefficient

Any other thoughts? Or should I just head back to JAGS?

Kris

> Invalid value of prec: Error in function validate transformed params N4stan5agrad3varE: prec[1] is 1.#QNAN:0, but must be greater than or equal to 0

I missed that in the last mail because it didn't wrap.
(I really need a new mailer.)

You're right that it's saying that the transformed parameter
prec[1] is NaN.

> And again, since I set prec[1] initially (see my above code), I don't know why I would keep getting this error over and
> over.

If prec_1 gets a non-negative value in the data file, the above error
shouldn't happen.

Can you send me the data so I can try to replicate the behavior?

Are you running Stan 1.3 in R?

- Bob

P.S. Sorry we haven't figured out a way around this clunky coding
convention if you want to specify one value of what would otherwise
be a vector of parameters. When we can slice on the left side of
an assignment it should at least be easier to code.
